- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to match true decline.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast slope by 10–20% after sentiment drops below 0.33.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is > 20% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently 2–3% below forecast, model is overconfident; apply a “sentiment-adjusted floor” rule: set lower bound at 10% below recent 18-day average if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
